analysis_notes.source_text_analysis: Torah #270 is a two-sentence teaching describing two forms of spiritual awakening (hitorerrut): one sparked by witnessing a fellow's fervent prayer, and one self-generated through one's own words of supplication. The text contains no bechina language whatsoever — no phrase 'בְּחִינַת', 'הוּא בְּחִינַת', or 'נִקְרָא' appears. All conceptual movement in the text is sequential/causal (eitza): prayer with a broken heart leads to crying 'vai li', which triggers self-examination ('heikhan ani'), which triggers a deeper and more personal crying. Because there are no bechina statements, there are no parallel-nature equivalences to encode as nodes, and no packages can be built from this Torah.
